# Studio

A design studio's proof sheet, caught mid-build: cool studio-white paper with an ink dot grid and a fine grain, blue-black ink, Hedvig Letters Serif for the heads (a contemporary serif with a calligraphic hand in its joins), a clean Geist body, crop marks at the corners of every printed piece, and one cadmium orange that both fills the action and draws the construction: metric guides, clear-space boxes, redlines. It reads as considered because the type is shown being measured. It is not a warm cream portfolio with a terracotta accent, and not a grey minimal template.

## Tokens

```css
:root {
  --color-paper: oklch(97.2% 0.006 215); --color-paper-2: oklch(94% 0.009 215); --color-paper-3: oklch(90.5% 0.011 215); --color-paper-hi: oklch(99% 0.004 215);
  --color-ink: oklch(16% 0.032 250); --color-ink-2: oklch(34% 0.022 245); --color-muted: oklch(49% 0.018 240);
  --color-rule: oklch(84% 0.010 225);
  --color-accent: oklch(68% 0.172 50); --color-accent-ink: oklch(16% 0.032 250); --color-focus: oklch(52% 0.15 48);
  --color-dot: color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-ink) 20%, transparent); --color-mark: color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-ink) 72%, transparent);
  --font-display: "Hedvig Letters Serif", ui-serif, Georgia, serif; --font-body: "Geist", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-outlier: "Sofia Sans Extra Condensed", "Arial Narrow", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif;
  --radius-card: 3px; --radius-pill: 3px; --rule-hair: 1px;
  --shadow-card: none;
  --shadow-sheet: 1px 2px 0 color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-ink) 7%, transparent), 10px 18px 36px -14px color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-ink) 32%, transparent);
  --tracking-display: -0.022em; --display-weight: 400;
}
```

## Type

- **Display:** Hedvig Letters Serif 400, its one weight, `--tracking-display`, line-height 0.98 to 1.04, sentence case, `font-optical-sizing: auto`. The hand holds from a 200px wordmark down to a 25px item title (tracking -0.005em there). Heads, figures and the wordmark only.
- **Body:** Geist 400 and 500, line-height 1.55, ink-2 for running text.
- **Labels, captions, guide readouts:** Geist 500 a step smaller, sentence case, `--color-muted`, tabular figures for any measurement. No mono.
- **Specimen face:** Sofia Sans Extra Condensed 500, only inside a specimen that shows an alternative system; never a head or label of the page itself.

## Surfaces

- The ground is a generated proof, never a picture: a 24px radial-gradient dot grid in `--color-dot` under an `feTurbulence` grain (`--grain`), on the hero, nav and footer, masked to fade before the next section; the rest of the page is clean paper.
- Crop marks on every printed piece (a sheet, a photograph, a card, a control, a focused field): eight 1px `--color-mark` ticks drawn with background gradients on a `::before`, set off the corners by a small gap, larger on a sheet. Registration targets may sit at a sheet's sides.
- Orange draws construction: 1px `--color-accent` guides at the font's real ascender, cap height, x-height, baseline and descender with their readouts in the label voice, a clear-space box in x units, redlines with dimensions. Rules only, never orange type.
- Two rules: 1px `--color-rule` between rows; 1px `--color-ink` opening a set. Radius 3px.
- One shadow, for paper objects only (a card, a sheet), lit from the top left: `--shadow-sheet`. Everything else lies flat.
- Bands: paper-2, or one ink band with paper type; never an orange field.
- Photographs: the work where it is used, level, daylight, verticals straight, true colour, crop-marked, a ratio redline beside it; never a mockup.

## Range

- **A wordmark under construction:** the name set huge in Hedvig with its metric guides, clear-space box and readouts on the dot grid; the pointer measures a letter's advance in font units.
- **Systems as specimen cards:** two or three alternatives as crop-marked cards (face line, `Aa Gg Rr 0123456789`, hex swatches) that switch one board set by type, colour or grid.
- **An index that opens:** rows under an ink rule, Hedvig at item size, each opening into a case with its photograph held at a stated ratio.
- **A size test:** one line at falling sizes (banner, poster, ticket), each on its own orange guides with its live size beside it.

## Controls

- Printed controls: a 1px ink border at 2px radius, a second rule inset 2px inside it, crop marks at the corners that open slightly on hover; the primary is filled orange with ink text. Geist 500, 48px.
- Fields: 3px, a 1px `--color-muted` border, crop marks appear on focus. Links take an orange underline on hover.
- Orange fill stays on the one action; orange lines are construction and may be many but thin.

## Motion

Guides draw in once along their length. A set of systems may turn every few seconds while in view and stops on any choice. State changes at `--dur-short` on `--ease-out`. Reduced motion: the full construction, still.

## Voice

Spare and exact, a little literary. Verbs over adjectives; name the work, the institution, the surface it lives on, the measurement. Never "creative solutions" or "brands brought to life".

## Do-nots

- Never Hedvig in running text, never the specimen face outside a specimen.
- Never an orange flood, orange type or a second warm colour.
- Never warm paper; the ground is cool, hue 215.
- Never a guide that is not true to the font's metrics or a dimension that is not the real one.
- Never the dot grid behind a whole page or running text.

# Blueprint

A drafting sheet as a material: Prussian-blue paper, a white line for ink, Chakra Petch drafted capitals over IBM Plex Sans, mono measurements with their units, keylines instead of cards, and photographs printed as cyanotypes, the sheet's blue in the shadows and its white in the light. It reads technical because everything is a line, a dimension or a print on one ground and the line is the only signal. It is not a dark product page with a blue gradient, not a neon wireframe.

## Tokens

```css
:root {
  --color-paper: oklch(35% 0.105 256); --color-paper-2: oklch(31% 0.10 257); --color-paper-3: oklch(26.5% 0.095 258);
  --color-ink: oklch(97% 0.012 240); --color-ink-2: oklch(90% 0.025 242); --color-muted: oklch(80% 0.045 244);
  --color-rule: oklch(93% 0.02 240 / 0.85); --color-rule-2: oklch(93% 0.02 240 / 0.32);
  --color-grid: oklch(97% 0.01 240 / 0.09); --color-grid-2: oklch(97% 0.01 240 / 0.2);
  --color-accent: oklch(97% 0.012 240); --color-accent-ink: oklch(33% 0.105 256); --color-focus: oklch(97% 0.012 240);
  --font-display: "Chakra Petch", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; --font-body: "IBM Plex Sans", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif;
  --font-outlier: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, monospace;
  --radius-card: 0; --radius-pill: 0; --rule-hair: 1px; --rule-heavy: 2px; --shadow-card: none;
  --tracking-display: -0.012em; --display-weight: 600; --sheet-inset: 20px; --tick: 14px;
}
```

Three sheets, stated in the stamp (`blueprint: cyanotype`).

| Sheet | Ground, line, muted |
| --- | --- |
| **cyanotype** (default) | the tokens above |
| **whiteprint** | ground `oklch(97.5% 0.006 240)`, ink `oklch(35% 0.105 256)`, muted `oklch(52% 0.07 255)` |
| **brownline** | ground `oklch(86% 0.045 80)`, ink `oklch(28% 0.05 50)`, muted `oklch(45% 0.05 55)`, a red pencil `oklch(45% 0.19 28)` for annotation only |

## Type

- **Display:** Chakra Petch 600 for every head, `--tracking-display`, roman, one weight a head: the h1 and h2 uppercase at line-height 1.02 (55a), the h3 in sentence case.
- **Body:** IBM Plex Sans 400 for prose and 500 for labels and controls; reversed on the sheet, nothing lighter than 400.
- **Labels, captions, table heads, meta:** IBM Plex Sans 500 a step smaller, sentence case. IBM Plex Mono 500 sets a measurement with its unit, a stage or drawing number, a year on a dimension string and code, nothing else.

## Surfaces

- Lines only: 1px `--color-rule` keylines on every surface, and a second keyline in `--color-rule-2` 5px inside on a figure or a photograph. Radius 0, no shadows; depth is a second line, a `--rule-heavy` line or a one-step darker ground.
- The dimension string: a hairline with a 45° tick (`--tick` long) at each end and short extension lines, its value set above it. It measures something real, never a decoration.
- The grid: 24px minor lines in `--color-grid`, 120px major in `--color-grid-2`, offset by `--sheet-inset`, only under a drawing, a schedule or a chart of real data.
- Bands: `--color-paper-2` or `--color-paper-3`, two a page at most; the sheet is already the colour (drenched), so there is no other field.
- Photographs: structures built and building, shot square-on so they read like drawings (a frame going up, a roof from below, a model on a table), printed as cyanotypes inside the double keyline; pick frames with a real white and a real shadow, since grey prints flat. Type over one sits on a `--color-paper-3` scrim from its edge.

## Range

- **Figures as dimensions:** the prompt's one number in Chakra Petch at display size, set on a dimension string that spans ten or twelve columns between its two real ends (a first year and now, a smallest and largest span), the ends in mono.
- **Tables as drawing registers:** a stage schedule, a deliverables list or a price list as a keylined table, stage numbers in mono in their own column, the row title one weight heavier, a `--rule-heavy` line under the head row; on `--color-paper-2` it reads as the register sheet of a set.
- **Forms as a title block:** fields set as cells of a keylined block, each label at the cell's top left, the cells sized by what they hold, the submit in the ink fill at the block's foot.
- **Comparisons and steps as elevations:** two options side by side as columns parted by one heavy line, or stages as a run along one long dimension string with a tick at each stage, each stage a numeral, a title and a line.

## Controls

- An ink-filled primary with sheet-coloured text beside a 1px-outlined secondary in ink, both square, 48px, IBM Plex Sans 500.
- Links in ink with a 1px underline that clears on hover; inputs square, 48px, a 1px `--color-rule` keyline on `--color-paper-2`, the white focus ring, never a glow.
- The line is the accent: white on blue, in rules, the primary fill and the focus ring.

## Motion

Static, drafted. A rule or a dimension string may draw itself once a page (scaleX from its left tick over `--dur-long` on `--ease-out`); hover on a keylined surface that links darkens its ground one step.

## Voice

Specification voice: the building type, the stage, the year, the format, a unit on every figure; nothing a drawing note could not carry.

## Do-nots

- Never a filled card, a blur or a lifted panel; the sheet has lines, not layers.
- Never a second colour on the cyanotype, in type or in a photograph; the red pencil belongs to the brownline sheet.
- Never a building, frame or section drawn to stand in for a project, and never a dimension string with an invented value; a drawing is real project data or it is absent.
- Never the grid as wallpaper behind prose, and never a lowercase h1 or h2.
- Never a rounded corner, anywhere.

## 05 · Workbench

Real product captures are the primary content. The page is a guided tour of the app in use, with short captions in place of marketing copy.

- **Heading:** plain and functional at the section size; the captures do the talking.
- **Body:** a sequence of capture blocks, each a `<figure>` with a `<figcaption>` that states a fact and one inline annotation.
- **Divider:** the figure is the divider; sections separate by gap and figure.
- **Button:** the hero's one action (44b), then, where the theme allows a sticky element, a bottom bar carrying it after the third capture, labelled with the verb ("Start a project").
- **Image:** the real capture, unframed, in a `<figure>`; until the user supplies it, the product built in a `data-slot` (`imagery.md` § 4). No browser or device chrome (47a, 47b).
- **Reveal:** one type-unmask, on the first caption; the captures load instantly and the rest is simply there.

Reach for it for SaaS, developer tools, editor extensions, anywhere seeing the product in use is the sale.

Avoid when the product is conceptual or services-led. Workbench needs a UI to show.

Compositions: Showcase and Split for the captures, a Band for the close (`layout.md` § 5); the optional bar is a sticky bottom bar with one action at `--z-sticky`.

**Sample opening lines** (imitate the specificity; the page walks the visitor through):
> *"$ streampipe parse access.log --filter status=5xx | jq"* Opens on a real command, not a claim.
> *"Read anything that emits lines: files, pipes, sockets, kubectl logs."* Names the inputs, refuses abstraction.
> *"Open the trace, find the span, fix the regression."* Three concrete verbs.

# Anatomy What a page is built around, by the visitor's job. Read the one job the prompt names at Step 2, before the shape: it sets where the action lives, which sections are the category's own, and how the page ends. The theme dresses this anatomy; the shape orders it; neither replaces it. Drawn from the homepages of about fifty real independent sites across these jobs; the pattern Hallmark slipped into (text beside a picture, a figure row, three steps, an email band) is how software pages look and almost nothing else. **When the prompt gives none of a section's content,** build it as a sample the user replaces, the way the product is built when it cannot be captured (`imagery.md` § 4): an example issue with its parts, dishes typical of the cuisine, three candles named plainly, track titles as placeholders, each marked in the handoff. A sample shows the shape of the real thing; it never states a fact a visitor could take as true (a price, a date, a person's name, a count, a review). A section whose whole content would be facts nobody gave (a lineup, a tour) is one line and a text slot, or it waits. Practical facts the job wants and the prompt lacks (hours, an address, dates) share the page's two missing-fact slots (`craft.md` § 8): slot the two a visitor needs to act. Every job: the nav carries the job's own action word (Book, Tickets, Shop, Listen, Start free), the hero shows the thing itself (the room, the cover, the dates, the screen), and proof comes in the category's own form, never a generic band of numbers. ## subscribe (a newsletter, a waitlist, a podcast) - **Action:** in the hero, and often it is the hero: the name, one line, the email field. A podcast puts the latest episode with its play control under it. - **Sections:** a sample issue or the latest one, set as it arrives; who writes it; the archive as an Index of issues or episodes with dates; the reader count only if given, set like a circulation figure under the masthead. - **Ends:** a second field under the archive, or the archive itself. The one job whose close may be an email field. ## book (a restaurant, a class, a clinic, a studio) - **Action:** a booking picker (party, date, time) opened from the nav and the hero, or the next free times as buttons; repeated beside the menu or the classes, never only at the foot. - **Sections:** the room or the food as a photograph with little or no head; the menu (a Switcher by lunch and dinner, or rows with prices); for classes the timetable as a Schedule; how to find it; hours and address as a section of their own. - **Ends:** hours, address and the booking again. A fine room may have almost nothing: one photograph, the menu, the booking. ## visit (a shop, a gallery, a venue, a place) - **Action:** today's hours and the address, in the nav or the hero; tickets or donate only if the prompt has them. - **Sections:** what is on now as the lead picture; what is coming as dated rows (an Index or a Schedule, a This week and Next week switch); for a shop, the shelves (a Rail or a Grid of the prompt's own things); getting there. - **Ends:** visit information and the address, or the mailing list for what is on next. ## attend (an event, a festival, a race, a conference) - **Action:** tickets in the nav from the first screen; the date and the place are the headline. - **Sections:** the lineup or the speakers (an Index or a dense Grid, the names set large); the days as a Schedule; ticket tiers with prices; the venue and travel; questions. Figures (stages, acts, miles) only when the prompt gives them. - **Ends:** tickets again, the questions, or the mailing list for the next edition. Between editions the whole page is the date, the place and the list. ## buy (a physical product, a small shop) - **Action:** the product with its price and options (an Offer), often as the hero; a buy action after the sections that earn it, or a sticky bar with the price. - **Sections:** the range as tiles or a Rail with prices; the product in use, close; how it is made; delivery and the guarantee as plain facts; reviews only if given. - **Ends:** the offer again, new arrivals, or the guarantee. An email field belongs in the footer, not as the close. ## try (an app, a game, a desktop tool) - **Action:** the store or download buttons right under the head, one per platform the prompt names. - **Sections:** the key art, trailer or main screen captured from the product (`imagery.md` § 4); features as named moments shown in screens (a Pinned run or a Switcher), not icon tiles; a before and after where the product changes something; platforms. - **Ends:** the download again beside one last screen. Games are short: five or six blocks is a full page. ## sign up (software, an API, a developer tool) - **Action:** start free in the nav and the hero with its terms in one line under it; for a developer tool the install command may be the action. - **Sections:** the product at work (captured or built); what it does as named moments; a code sample or the integration; the pricing table with its period switch; questions. - **Ends:** the hero's action again in a short band, or the code sample. Never a newsletter. ## hire (a studio, a freelancer, an architect) - **Action:** a plain contact (an email, a phone, "Talk to us") in the nav and once more after the work; no form needed. - **Sections:** the work as the page: a list or Index of projects (name, client, year, place) with pictures, one opened as a case; what the studio does as a short list; where it is. - **Ends:** contact details, per office if there are several. ## join (a club, a community, a membership) - **Action:** join or "your first visit" in the hero. - **Sections:** what a session is like, shown; when and where as a Schedule or a list of places; membership options as rows with prices; first-visit guidance; people in the prompt's own pictures only. - **Ends:** the first visit, the membership options, or a sign-up field. ## listen (a band, a film, a podcast, a publication) - **Action:** the new release or current issue with its listen, watch or order buttons side by side. - **Sections:** the record, film or issue (its cover, its tracks or contents as an Index); dates (tour, screenings) as rows with ticket links; earlier work as covers in a Rail or Grid; videos. - **Ends:** the dates, more of the catalogue, or the mailing list. Artist pages can be very short: one picture, the release, the dates. With no release in the prompt, the act leads instead (the players, how it sounds described plainly, where it plays) and the page's job is booking them: the close is the enquiry. ## How pages end In the order real sites use them: the hero's action again in a short band; practical details (hours, address, contacts); more of the catalogue (the archive, new arrivals, more work); a short trust tail (a guarantee, press, awards the prompt gives); a mailing list, for things that recur (issues, editions, releases, events). The last is one close in five, never the default (85). ==== # Patterns The parts every page repeats, written to pass the gates. Take the code's shape; the names, copy, values and composition are yours. `tokens.css`, `base.css` and the slot script come from the scaffold. ## Controls, all eight states ```css .btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-xs); min-height: 48px; padding: 0 var(--space-lg); border: 1px solid var(--color-ink); border-radius: var(--radius-input, var(--radius-pill)); background: var(--color-ink); color: var(--color-paper); font: 500 var(--text-md)/1 var(--font-body); white-space: nowrap; text-decoration: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color var(--dur-short) var(--ease-out), transform var(--dur-micro) var(--ease-out); } .btn:hover { background: var(--color-ink-2); } .btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus); outline-offset: 2px; } .btn:disabled, .btn[aria-disabled="true"] { opacity: 0.55; cursor: not-allowed; transform: none; } .btn[aria-busy="true"] { cursor: progress; } .btn--quiet { background: transparent; color: var(--color-ink); border-color: var(--color-rule); } .btn--quiet:hover { background: var(--color-paper-2); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .btn { transition: background-color var(--dur-short) linear; } } ``` One filled primary a page (F4); the quiet one goes somewhere else. Error and success belong to the form, below. ## A photograph in a slot ```html

Picking runs from September to the first frost.

``` ```css .photo { aspect-ratio: 4 / 5; min-height: 440px; margin: 0; border-radius: var(--radius-card); } .photo > img { outline: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-ink) 8%, transparent); outline-offset: -1px; } .caption { margin-top: var(--space-sm); font-size: var(--text-sm); color: var(--color-ink-2); } ``` The `` comes from `theme.mjs photos`; `base.css` supplies the cover fit, the loading wash and the theme's treatment. The credit goes in the footer's *Photographs* line; the caption is a fact from the prompt, outside the frame. A product sample takes the same kind of slot with no ``: the interface built at full size (`imagery.md` § 4). ## A choice between a few ```html
Size
``` ```css .seg input { position: absolute; opacity: 0; width: 1px; height: 1px; } .seg label { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 var(--space-md); border: 1px solid var(--color-rule); cursor: pointer; } .seg input:checked + label { background: var(--color-ink); color: var(--color-paper); } .seg input:focus-visible + label { outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus); outline-offset: 2px; } ``` The radios stay in the flow at one pixel (53); the label carries the state and the ring, in the body face, sentence case. ## A rail and a switcher ```html
  • 12 June Whitby
...
...
``` ```css .rail { display: grid; grid-auto-flow: column; grid-auto-columns: minmax(16rem, 22%); gap: var(--gap-columns); overflow-x: auto; scroll-snap-type: x mandatory; scroll-padding-inline: var(--gutter); padding-inline: var(--gutter); overscroll-behavior-x: contain; } .rail > * { scroll-snap-align: start; } .rail:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus); outline-offset: 4px; } ``` The rail scrolls by touch, wheel and arrow keys once focused, and sits outside the container's padding so its edge cuts the next item. The switcher's tabs move with the arrow keys (a few lines of script set `aria-selected`, `tabindex` and `hidden`); without script every panel shows in order. A pinned pair is `position: sticky; top: var(--space-2xl)` on the visual's column, released under 60rem. ## A fact the prompt did not give ```html

Doors at time to be announced, at the venue.

``` ```css .fill { padding: 0 0.25em; border: 1px dashed color-mix(in oklch, var(--color-muted) 70%, transparent); border-radius: 3px; color: var(--color-muted); -webkit-box-decoration-break: clone; box-decoration-break: clone; } ``` Two a page at most, each named in the handoff (`craft.md` § 8). ## A form that posts nowhere yet ```html

# Craft Type, colour, surfaces, motion, copy, section openings, missing facts and finish, read on every page build, as numbers wherever a number exists. `layout.md` owns the canvas, the sizes, the sections and the hero; `imagery.md` owns the pictures; the theme supplies the material. ## 1. Type At most two families, a display face and a body face (one family may do both). A third is one **outlier** with exactly one role (a wordmark, a headline figure, code; mono for code and measured figures counts as one); a second role makes it a third family in running use (37, F13). One family at different weights is one family. - **Weights:** three at most across the page, display and body together (F19), picked as extremes: 300 beside 800, or 400 beside 700. - **Sizes:** on a theme build, the roles in `layout.md` § 2, built on a 1.25 ratio from a 16px body, plus a wordmark size if the theme names one; a custom build sets its own scale from the scaffold's (`direction.md` § Mechanics). Hierarchy past those comes from weight and colour. - **Display:** tracking -0.02 to -0.04em on a regular-width face, 0 to -0.015em on a condensed or very heavy one (two letters touching is a fault); line-height 1.0 to 1.15, tighter as it grows (1.2 reads as inherited; a mixed-case poster head may close to 0.92). An uppercase head that can wrap never goes under 1.0 (55a). A head is one weight, one style and one colour: one word set apart by italic, colour, weight or a highlight is the accented word (38i, 38iii); stress comes from a line break or a second line at a second size. - **Display size:** `--text-display` (84px at 1440); a theme may set 5.5rem, 6rem when display-heavy, 7rem for a single word. A poster-scale theme or shape (Manifesto, Marquee Hero, a Poster hero) sizes with the screen, `clamp(4rem, 10vw, 9rem)`, full size at 1440 and held at 1920 (Floor 14), while the fold still holds the headline, one sentence and the action. A wide face takes the poster scale a step down. - **Headline by length:** count the rendered `h1`: 20 characters or fewer, full display (a single word may reach 7rem); 21 to 50, display; 51 to 90, `--text-display-s` or split at the sense break with `
`; over 90, rewrite. A `
` goes only between phrases and is checked at 375, where it often lands badly; heads take `text-wrap: balance`, body copy `pretty`, so no head ends on a stub and no paragraph on one word (F26). - **Heading measure** rides on the element in `ch` (the scaffold sets `h1` 20ch, `h2` 30ch, `h3` 40ch; a head at display-s about 24ch), never on the heading group's wrapper. - **Body:** 16px minimum, line-height 1.5 to 1.65, measure 45 to 75ch (25); never all caps, never justified without hyphenation (F22), never tracked past 0.05em. - **Labels, captions, table heads, meta, tags, chips, nav links:** the body face a step smaller, sentence case (lowercase on a theme whose voice is lowercase), untracked (67). Mono only for code, a figure or a measurement, or when mono is the theme's material (64). Capitals belong to a wordmark and to a theme whose display voice is uppercase, where a control may follow at 0.04em or less. - **Required:** `font-display: swap`; a fallback of the same build (a grotesk to `system-ui`, a serif to Georgia), metric overrides only where published; `font-synthesis: none`, only the weights you use; `tabular-nums` on figures that compare (F6); `text-wrap: balance` on heads (F3) and `pretty` on body; curly quotes, a true ellipsis, a non-breaking space inside unit pairs (`10 MB`, `⌘ K`) in a proportional face. - **Wordmark:** may take another face than the body, and on tone-rich themes should (`fonts.md` § The wordmark); one family throughout only when the body voice is the brand (a letter, a manifesto, a long document). ## 2. Colour - **OKLCH everywhere.** - **Four layers.** Paper (light: L 92 to 98, chroma 0.005 to 0.015 toward the anchor hue; dark: L 12 to 18, 0.008 to 0.015). Ink (on light paper L 16 to 24, on dark L 88 to 96, tinted 0.005 to 0.014). Five to nine neutrals between them, each tinted 0.005 to 0.018 (22). One accent at chroma 0.12 to 0.22 with a paired `--color-accent-ink` (41). A focus colour on the accent's hue, chroma 0.18 to 0.22, L within 5% of the accent. - **Never a pure absolute** as a surface or an improvised value (7a, 7b); tint the greys toward the anchor. - **The accent is a signal, not a fill:** under 5% of any viewport under the default Restrained posture (23): an active nav item, a focus ring, a link underline on hover, the primary control, the one series a chart argues from. - **Postures,** declared in the stamp before code. **Restrained** (above). **Committed:** one colour carries 30 to 60% of the surface through `--color-field` or the paper family; the accent stays a signal. **Full palette:** three or four named roles (field, signal, seal, ink), each with a job and a footprint. **Drenched:** the surface is the colour; ink and rules derive from it. A declared surface colour is not accent footprint. - **Contrast:** body 4.5:1 (target 7:1) or APCA Lc 60; large text, icons, focus rings and field edges 3:1 or Lc 45 (40). Every rule that paints a dark surface swaps its text colour in the same rule (41); grey text never sits on a coloured surface. - **Bans:** gradients past three stops; purple-blue, purple-pink or cyan-on-dark anywhere (2a); glow shadows on dark, chromatic halos, spotlights (29); alpha as a colour's definition (alpha is for overlays and shadows); red and green as the only signal. - **Dark mode** is opt-in and derived, never inverted (`dark-mode.md`). ## 3. Surfaces - **A primary axis:** left-biased, right-biased, top-heavy or bottom-weighted. Centre-biased is a default, not a choice (6b). - **Spacing is a scale:** `--space-3xs` 2px · `2xs` 4 · `xs` 8 · `sm` 12 · `md` 16 · `lg` 24 · `xl` 40 · `2xl` 64 · `3xl` 96 · `4xl` 144. A raw length where a token exists fails (24a); at most three optical nudges off the scale (24b). `gap` for siblings, `margin` only to break the flow. - **Grids:** CSS Grid for the page, Flexbox inside components; flex children that must shrink take `min-width: 0`, icons and images `flex-shrink: 0`. No empty cell and no orphan on a last row: change the count (F20). Grids hold their column count above 1440, and `vw` visuals carry a `max-width` (44d). - **The surface ladder:** whitespace, then a hairline (1px `--color-rule`), then a tinted well (`--color-paper-2` or `-3`, no border), then a card (a border or a shadow, never both, F24), kept for content that is independently interactive or of a different kind. Never white cards on a tinted page, a card in a card (4), or a bordered box inside a well; climb different rungs at different seams (9, F7). Sibling stats part with a top or vertical hairline: no leading padding on the first, no trailing on the last, the pattern reset wherever the column count changes. - **Depth is weight and scale.** One shadow at most: `0 1px 2px oklch(20% 0.01 / 0.05)` or `0 0 0 1px oklch(30% 0.01 / 0.06)`. Elevated surfaces are never darker than their canvas. Eight z levels: base 1, raised 10, dropdown 100, sticky 200, sticky-nav 300, modal 400, toast 500, tooltip 600 (56). - **Clipping:** `overflow-x: clip` keeps `sticky` and `fixed` working where `hidden` breaks them (34); the section holding a deliberate overflow keeps `overflow: visible`. - **Radii:** one per level, concentric (`inner = outer - padding`, at least 2px); image radii `min(1vw, var(--radius-card))`. ## 4. The hero's motion Size, posture and composition are `layout.md` § 6; what it shows is `imagery.md` § 1. - **Entrance:** one settle of 0.4 to 0.8s including its stagger, from an already-visible default; a fade with an 8px rise is one motion. Never a fade, a sweep and a scale on one element; never bounce; never a starfield, a mouse parallax or an auto-rotating carousel. - **Before it ships,** the hero's visual shows the real thing, is big, keeps the accent under its footprint and weighs under 2 MB with a reduced-motion fallback; any no changes the visual, never the copy. ## 5. Motion - **Who decides:** the theme's Motion section; a shape's reveal runs only where the theme allows one, the genre's default only where the theme is silent. - **Only `transform` and `opacity`** (10a); blur, `clip-path`, mask and shadow may join when they stay smooth on the element alone. - **Easings:** `--ease-out` for arrivals, `--ease-in` for exits, `--ease-in-out` for toggles; never the browser's `ease`, `linear` only for progress and scrubbing, no overshoot on UI state (12). - **Durations:** `--dur-micro` 120ms (press, tick, colour), `--dur-short` 220ms (hover, tooltip, menu), `--dur-long` 420ms (modal, drawer, accordion, reveal). Exits at 60 to 75% of the enter. Stagger 30 to 50ms between rows, 60 to 100ms between blocks, 500ms in all at most, once. - **One reveal per page,** staggered by `--i`, 0.4 to 0.8s in all, content visible without it (62; `patterns.md` § One reveal). Under reduced motion every reveal shows its end state at once and the render tier shoots that way; what must still run (a loader, a 150ms fade) takes `.keep-motion`. - **Scroll:** IntersectionObserver for reveals and threshold states; a passive, frame-throttled scroll listener only where direction matters; scroll-scrubbed motion only as one pattern from `scroll-choreography.md` (F8). - **State:** hover is one signal (11) that raises contrast: a colour step, or a 1px lift at micro on a control that keeps its colour. Tooltips wait 800 to 1000ms on hover, 0 on focus (17); focus rings never animate (15); menus, modals and accordions follow `microinteractions.md`. - **Never:** parallax, custom cursors, cursor followers, a marquee that will not pause on hover and focus (18), `will-change` on a whole class, a pulsing dot, a caret blinking past five beats, an infinite loop other than a loader, one small loop of 4s or less, or one ambient loop the theme declares (8s or slower). Every loop stops under reduced motion and off-screen, and one past 5 seconds carries a visible pause control (`patterns.md` § A loop that can pause). ## 6. Copy Write as the owner would say it across a counter: the prompt's own nouns, a real place, a number the user gave, the verb a customer would use. - **The swap test:** a head that would work on a competitor's page is rewritten with a noun only this prompt has. *Software that works for you* fits anyone; *Invoices that chase themselves* fits one product. - **Three tests a line:** can the reader picture it, could it be proven false, could only this business say it. Specific beats clever: the place, the hour, the material, the result (*Sourdough at four, gone by ten*); a pun is a second-draft move, once a page at most. - **The subhead** says what it is, for whom and the one difference, in twelve words or fewer. **Section heads** say what the visitor will see or get (*Three loaves a morning*), never a category label (*Features*, *Our story*, *Why us*); a staged shape's one-word stage names are the exception. - **Rhythm:** a short line beside a longer one; verbs over adjectives; one idea a sentence; no triads of adjectives (*fast, simple, powerful*). - **Budget** (58): headlines seven words or fewer, section heads six or fewer; section intros one line; paragraphs two short sentences; lists four items of a three-word label and a ten-word line (five for steps that cannot merge; past that, a table); tables five rows; a set the user gave keeps its true count; 450 visible words a page at most. Read only the headings and the hero: if they tell the story, the rest is the right length. - **Refuse the generated voice:** everything gate 19 names, plus *Reimagine*, *Whether you're X or Y*, *It's not just X, it's Y*, *Say goodbye to*, *game-changer*, *journey*, a colon title (*Focus: the app for*), *Click here*, *Enter your email below*, a version string in marketing copy. - **Buttons:** the verb of the action (*Book a fitting*); *Continue* only as a flow's second step. **Errors:** what happened, why if known, what to do; no *Oops*, no exclamation marks. **Empty states:** what is empty, why it matters, one action. **Loading:** a spinner after 150 to 300ms, shown at least 300ms, beside the label; *Loading…* past 2s. - **Sample data** inside a built product uses `example.com`, the prompt's field names and values that read as samples (*Example Kitchen*, round amounts), never a figure a visitor could take as a claim (46a). - **Punctuation:** curly quotes, `…`, a true apostrophe, no `--` and no em or en dash (a comma, a colon, a full stop or parentheses instead), a non-breaking space before units. A full stop on every standalone sentence, none on list items. ## 7. Opening a section The reflex is a small tracked-caps label above the heading, and the reflex is the tell (54). Ask *what does the reader not yet know?* If nothing, open with nothing. If something, it rides on a fact, a destination or an identifier, never on a name for what comes next. Twelve ways in: 1. **Nothing:** air above, the heading flush. 2. **The heading announces itself:** the subject in its first two words. # Imagery What a page shows, read on every page build. A page looks made when it shows the real thing (the place, the food, the object, the hands at work, the product running), and generated when it shows a gradient box, a drawing of a loaf, or a heading with nothing under it. ## 1. What fills a page In order, the first that fits: 1. **The user's own images and recordings**, asked for at Step 1. They win every slot. 2. **Screenshots of the real product,** taken by the build itself whenever the product can be reached: a URL, a running dev server, a project in the folder that starts with one command, a desktop or phone app on this machine (§ 4). A real screen beats any picture of one. 3. **The product built,** only when there is no product to capture yet (§ 4). 4. **Photographs from the library**, picked by script and treated in the theme's way (§ 2, § 5). 5. **Generated stills**, only when `TOGETHER_API_KEY` is set and the user asked for them (§ 6). 6. **Type at full scale**, when the prompt is about words. Which prompts want which: - **A place, a material, food or drink, an object, a craft, the outdoors, an event, people at work** (a bakery, a ski school, a gin, a weaving studio, a venue, a tailor, a farm): photographs lead. The hero's photograph is the largest thing on the first screen (full-bleed behind the head, or beside it at 60 to 75% of the screen tall). After it, two to four more carry the page, one of them large, each on its subject (an off-subject picture is cut, never kept to fill a count), with sections of the material alone between them (a menu or price list as rows, the hours and the place as a table, a statement, a form), so pictures take a quarter to a third of the page (§ 5, 83). - **Software** (SaaS, an app, a developer tool): the product leads, and the hero visual is its interface. One or two photographs may set the scene (where it is used, the material it handles, hands at the work it serves) when each passes the deletion test: take it away and the page loses a fact. A city at night, a laptop on a desk or an office building fails it. - **Words** (docs, an API, a CLI, a type specimen, a manifesto or a letter about an idea): type and code carry it; one photograph as a full-bleed band at most. A manifesto or a letter about something physical (repair, a river, a street) shows it like any other page. A photograph never stands in for a fact: numbers, names and claims stay in type, and a picture of a person never stands in for a customer, a teammate or a testimonial (F9). ## 2. The library Hallmark carries 755 verified photographs from Wikimedia Commons, each CC0, public domain, CC BY or CC BY-SA, tagged by subject, tone and temperature. Ask for each subject the page needs, concretely: ``` node /scripts/theme.mjs photos "apple orchard in autumn" "hands picking apples" --theme [--n 3] [--orient portrait|landscape|square] [--seed ] [--log .hallmark/log.json] ``` It ranks the library for each subject, steers away from the photos the last five builds used, and prints for each pick what it shows, its size, a ready `` with its `srcset`, and its credit. Keep only picks that fit the sentence the section makes; re-ask in other words (the place, the material, the action) before settling for a near miss. - **Never write an image URL from memory or take one from a stock site** (Unsplash, Pexels and Pixabay bar AI-driven selection in their terms). Use only what the script printed or the user supplied (76). - **Credit every library photo:** one line in the footer marked `data-credits` (the word budget skips it), *Photographs:* then each printed credit, in the footer's small style. CC BY and CC BY-SA require it (76). - **Size and crop in CSS:** keep the printed `srcset`, set `sizes` to the layout (`50vw` for a half, `100vw` full-bleed), and crop with the frame: `aspect-ratio` on the slot, `object-fit: cover`, the printed `object-position` (or your own) to keep the subject in frame. - **For production,** `--save ` downloads the picks into the project and prints local paths; drafts may link the Commons thumbnails. - **The hero photograph is the LCP:** `fetchpriority="high"`, never `loading="lazy"`; every other image is lazy. A full-bleed or hero frame takes a photo 2400px or more on its long side; a smaller one goes soft at 1920. - **A stand-in stays swappable:** in its slot (§ 3), with `data-alt` naming what the user's own picture should show, listed in the handoff. - **No Node:** say so in the Picks block and use slots with the user's material only; never guess a file. ## 3. Slots A slot is any picture the user will replace: `data-slot=""` (`hero`, `demo-2`, `photo-1`), a `data-alt` saying what belongs there, and a real size (an `aspect-ratio` or a fixed height). The scaffold's `base.css` holds the slot CSS, and the scaffold prints the `hallmarkSlots` script: paste it once before `` (F18). It swaps in the user's files without touching the layout (`hallmarkSlots({ hero: 'shop.jpg' })`) and drops a stand-in that fails to load. - **A slot always shows something:** the user's image, a library photograph, or the product built at full fidelity. Its wash (`--color-paper-2` to `--color-paper-3`) is only the colour behind a photo while it loads; a slot showing nothing but its wash is an empty picture (81). - **No visible placeholder labels:** no "your screenshot here", ratio notes or "sample" chips; `data-alt` and the handoff carry that. - A child that must stay once the user's image lands (a credit, a plate number) carries `data-keep`; text over a slotted photograph (a Poster hero's head and scrim) sits in a sibling layer above the slot (`z-index: 2` or more; the slot's image takes 1), never inside it. - Never more than four slots in a row, and never a set of frames for things the page has no pictures of (a team, a list of venues): set those in type (68). ## 4. The product: captured first, built only when it cannot be **Capture it.** When the product exists, the page shows it, not a mock of it. Find it at Step 0: a URL in the prompt, a dev server already running, a `package.json` with a `dev` or `start` script, a built app on the machine, or a path the user names. Start it if it needs starting (install, run, wait for the port), put it in the state that tells the page's story (sample data, a real project open, the one screen that does the job), then: ``` node /scripts/capture.mjs http://localhost:3000 --routes /,/settings --sizes desktop,phone [--selector ".editor"] [--full] [--out images/screens] ``` It writes 2x PNGs at 1440 x 900 and 390 x 844 (or one element with `--selector`) and prints an `` for each. A desktop app built on Electron, WebView2 or CEF is started with a DevTools port and captured through it (`capture.mjs --cdp 9222 --target "" [--selector ...]`, clean and at its own pixel density); any other desktop app with the OS (`screencapture -l ` or `-R x,y,w,h` on macOS), a phone app with its simulator (`xcrun simctl io booted screenshot`), a terminal tool by running it and setting its real output in a code block. Look at every capture before it ships: nothing personal on screen (names, emails, tokens, file paths), no error states unless they are the point, no debug overlays. Use several: the main screen in the hero, a detail cropped large lower down, a second screen, the phone view. Stamp `imagery: screenshots (capture.mjs)` and credit nothing; they are the user's own. **Frame it in the theme.** A capture sits in a `data-slot` with the theme's radius and the inset outline (§ 5), never inside a drawn browser bar, device frame, traffic lights or notch (47a, 47b). Crop to the part that sells (`object-position`, or `--selector`), keep text in it legible at its displayed size (scale 2, never upscaled), and never retouch what the product shows. Captures are product pictures: mark their slots `data-kind="product"`, so they do not count toward the photo balance (83). **Build it only when it cannot be captured** (an idea, a product not built yet, nothing reachable): the hero visual is the product's main screen built in HTML and CSS: real controls, at least eight elements, the prompt's nouns, the theme's surfaces and type, at the size `layout.md` § 6 gives the visual. Sample values read as samples (`example.com`, *Example Kitchen*, round plausible amounts), never a figure a visitor could take as a claim (46a). It sits in a `data-slot` so the real screenshot replaces it, and the handoff says which screens to capture once the product runs. Never build a mock of a product the build could have captured (84). A working control (a calculator on the user's prices, a booking form) is a fine section and a fine close, once a page; it is not the default hero. ## 5. Placing and treating photographs - **Big or not at all.** A photograph spans six of twelve columns and stands 440px tall or more, or runs full-bleed; at thumbnail size it reads as clip art (a set of four or more may run smaller, each with its fact). In the hero it stands 60 to 75% of the screen tall beside the text, or fills the screen behind the head (the Poster posture). Delete the picture in your head: if the screen still says the same thing, the picture is too weak or too small. - **One subject a frame, cropped tight,** its weight leaning toward the text. Vary the ratio (4:5 beside text, 16:9 or 21:9 across, 1:1 in a pair) and the size (8 and 4 columns; three equal frames only for a true set: three dishes, three rooms). - **Balance.** Below the hero, photographs take at most a third of the page at 1440 (pictures inside the built product, marked `data-kind="product"`, do not count), up to 45% on a Photographic or Portfolio Grid shape; past that the page reads as a stock gallery and the theme never speaks (83). Never two photograph-led sections in a row: follow a picture with a section the theme's type, rules, colour or the product carry alone (the theme file's Range). A software page alternates the product with type-led sections and takes one or two photographs; a word-led page takes one at most. When in doubt, cut the weakest picture and set its fact large. - **Text over a photograph** sits on its calmest part over a scrim from the theme's ink (a gradient from the text's edge, 35 to 65%), behind the text's side only, at 4.5:1 or better against the image under it; never centred white type over a busy frame. A theme that refuses gradients uses a solid ink plate. - **Facts on the pictures:** captions are facts from the prompt in the label style, beside or under the picture (the dish and its price, the room and its hours, the date, the place). Never a credit line there, and never a caption that claims a stand-in as the user's own person, place or product. - **The theme's treatment, on every photo.** The theme's `photo:` header sets it and the scaffold writes it into `base.css` as CSS on every image in a slot, the user's own included: `natural`, `warm`, `muted`, `mono`, `duotone` in two of the theme's tokens, or `tint` in one, with adjustments (`con=`, `sat=`, `exp=`). A duotone or tint flattens a pale subject (snow, a white wall) into an empty field: choose frames with tonal range and look at each through the treatment. A duotone or tint takes the slot's `::before`, so draw a keyline or scrim with `::after` or a sibling. A photo inside a built product takes the treatment only if the page adds it. - **The frame is the theme's:** its radius, an inset outline of ink at 6 to 10% (`outline: 1px solid ...; outline-offset: -1px`), its texture if it has one. Never a border and a wide shadow together (F24). ## 6. Generated stills Only when `TOGETHER_API_KEY` is set and the user asked for generated images, or for a subject the library cannot reach: `comp.md` § Generated stills. Never auto-fire it. ## 7. Never - **A drawn illustration** (80): an SVG or CSS figure of an object, plant, animal, person, product, building, landscape or scene past icon size. SVG is for icons from one set, the user's logo, charts and diagrams of real data or a real system with their labels, and plain geometry (a rule, a grid, a dot pattern as texture). - **An empty picture** (81): a slot showing only its wash, or a gradient field where a picture should be. - **A counting device** (82): a row or grid of identical marks standing for a quantity, one for each bottle or day. Set the number. - **Illustration packs and characters:** unDraw, Humaaans, Storyset, Lottie mascots, 3D blobs, isometric scenes. - Stock faces as proof (F9); a logo wall without the user's logos (46a); mesh blobs, orbs or aurora behind text (29); an image that zooms or rotates on hover (11); text baked into a picture; a photo of a screen showing someone else's interface. ## 8. Icons, logos, video, 3D - **Icons:** one library a page (Lucide by default; Phosphor or Heroicons in a project that uses them), one stroke width and one style, at 16, 20, 24 or 32px on the set's grid (a 24 viewBox at 24px, never scaled to 19), `currentColor`, aligned to the first line of multi-line text, never in a coloured tile (3, F5), never an emoji (30a). A button with an icon pads the icon side by the vertical padding. - **Logos:** the user's own, monochrome, one treatment a row, 32 to 48px tall (20 to 28px in a footer); Simple Icons (`https://cdn.simpleicons.org//`) only for a platform or brand the page names. Never an invented wall (46a). - **Video:** the user's recording or footage: `autoplay muted loop playsinline` with a `poster` (28a, 28b), AV1 or VP9 WebM then H.264 MP4, under 2 MB for ten seconds, a visible pause control on any loop past five seconds, captions when it speaks. - **3D and WebGL** only when the product is 3D and the visitor handles it, with a still fallback. - **Motion libraries:** CSS and `@property` first; Motion for orchestrated entrances in React; GSAP only when a timeline is the product. ## 9. Stamp, log and handoff Stamp `imagery: photographs, library 5, mono · product sample in hero and demo-2` (or `imagery: none`); the log's `imagery` field carries the same words and `photos` the ids used, so the next build's picks rotate. The handoff lists every stand-in and built sample with its slot, its size and what the user's own picture should show.

==== 11-catalogue
## 11 · Catalogue

Uniform grid of variations of the same thing: typefaces, palettes, SKUs. The page is a visual index of inventory.

- **Heading:** one line at the theme's display scale over the grid; the products lead, so the heading never pushes the first row below the fold.
- **Body:** a grid of same-sized cards, 3 to 5 per row, each one variant of the core product; image tracks `minmax(0, 1fr)` (50).
- **Divider:** hairline rules between rows.
- **Button:** a link inside each card to its detail page; no global CTA. The fold's one visible action is the first card's link (44b).
- **Image:** a specimen thumbnail or a swatch per card when the user gave the images; otherwise a library photograph of the kind of thing, or each card set in type (the name, the one fact, the price, a colour swatch where colour is the variant), never a row of empty frames (68).
- **Reveal:** none.

Reach for it for foundries, palette tools, font shops, colour systems, capsule collections.

Avoid for narrative brands. Catalogue treats every item as equal, wrong for a product with hierarchy.

Compositions: Grid (`layout.md` § 5), one card per item: its image, name, price and one action.

**Sample opening lines** (inventory headers: dated, with a count):
> *"Today's loaves."* Two words, ownership of the day (Maple Street Bread).
> *"Five collections, in store now."* The count and the where.
> *"Thirty-eight pieces this spring, every one hand-stitched."* Count, season, qualifier; no adjectives.
==== 15-split-studio
## 15 · Split Studio

Diptych. Every major block divides the screen, text on one side, proof on the other, and the proof keeps its side down the page (one mirror at most, never a zigzag, `layout.md` § 7).

- **Heading:** half the screen wide; the other half holds a capture or a supplied quote.
- **Body:** text-and-proof rows that vary by weight, not by side: one lead row gives the proof the larger share, the rest split evenly; one column gap for all of them (F15).
- **Divider:** a clear gutter between halves; no rules.
- **Button:** an outlined chip below the text half.
- **Image:** on the proof side in every row: a real capture, or the product built in a slot (`imagery.md` § 4).
- **Reveal:** the hero's two halves fade in once, 60 to 100ms apart; the rows below are simply there.

Reach for it for SaaS feature pages, developer tools that pair explanation with code, anything where every claim wants a visual proof.

Avoid for narrative or photographic brands. Split halves the attention; some pages need one focus.

Compositions: Split (`layout.md` § 5), the proof keeping its side.

**Sample opening lines** (a positioning statement paired with a proof column):
> *"A studio for what comes next."* Italic display beside a selected-work column.
> *"Print discipline, on screen."* Two phrases, set like a masthead.
> *"We design and build products for small ambitious teams."* Names the verbs and the audience.
==== 16-feature-stack
## 16 · Feature Stack

Sticky left pane holding the heading, scroll-synced right pane cycling through related captures. Paced like film.

- **Heading:** held inside the sticky pane; persists while content cycles beside it.
- **Body:** two columns, left sticky, right scrolling; the right pane plays through 3 to 6 detail captures per section.
- **Divider:** section bands; the sticky pane re-anchors per section, at `top: var(--banner-height)` under a sticky nav (56).
- **Button:** in the sticky pane, shown once the section's last capture is reached; with scripting off it is simply there (62).
- **Image:** the scrolling column is real captures, or the product built in slots until they arrive (`imagery.md` § 4); never a run of empty frames (68).
- **Reveal:** none of the fade kind; the sticky scroll is the motion. Choreograph it with [`../scroll-choreography.md`](../scroll-choreography.md) § 4 Sticky diptych with the pane kept on the left, or § 1 Pinned chapter: one pattern per page.

Reach for it for premium products, complex feature stories, anywhere the pacing should be controlled as the visitor scrolls.

Avoid for mobile-first audiences without a strong fallback. Sticky scroll-sync is rough on small screens.

Compositions: a pinned Split (`layout.md` § 5), the pin per `scroll-choreography.md` § 4.

Mobile: under 60rem the sticky pane becomes a heading above its captures, stacked in flow.

**Sample opening lines** (pin one statement, then walk the visitor through):
> *"Plan, build, ship."* Three verbs, three sticky panes.
> *"Read anything that emits lines."* Names what is possible, then walks through it (Streampipe).
> *"From stdin, through the pipe, into your dashboard."* Names the data path, then explains each step.
==== 18-portfolio-grid
## 18 · Portfolio Grid

Filterable cards of projects. Studio and designer homepages where the work is the product.

- **Heading:** a short line above the grid; no display.
- **Body:** a responsive grid of project cards, same size or with slight size variation; image tracks `minmax(0, 1fr)` (50).
- **Divider:** the filter row above the grid; no internal rules.
- **Button:** a link inside each card ("View the case study"); no global CTA. The fold's one visible action is the first card's link (44b).
- **Image:** a thumbnail per card, from the user's work; until it arrives, the projects are set in type with one slot at most (68).
- **Reveal:** card fade on filter change.

Reach for it for design studios, agencies, photographer portfolios, any creative business where the work is the pitch.

Avoid for products. Portfolio Grid is a service-business shape.

Compositions: Grid with a filter row (`layout.md` § 5).

**Sample opening lines** (name the volume and the era):
> *"Selected work, 2018 to 2026."* A date range, nothing else.
> *"Twelve projects, six clients, two countries."* Three counts, no adjective.
> *"Work, indexed by year."* The index is the whole site.

Better align-items: center. The tag is 20px tall, the button 48px; center. Good. On the primary button hover, the color change; the tag remains. Add it harmlessly: ```css .btn:disabled, .btn[aria-disabled="true"] { opacity:.55; cursor:not-allowed; transform:none; } ``` But no disabled buttons; the guard likely passes. Keep the GitHub links underlined (they're standalone). `.index__link { text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: var(--color-muted); }`. Focus ring on nav links: global outline, offset 2; the sticky bar's height 64, ring may overflow but fine. Careful: `--nav-h` is a raw 64px token; fine. The banner is above the nav; once the nav sticks, the anchor lands below it. Good. Mobile hero: the banner wraps to 2 lines (min-height 40 grows). The nav sticks below. Fine. Now, the "open to" banner on paper-2 with a border. The text 14px ink-2. Maybe add a mono label "STATUS"? No. Wait, gate 66: "a weather or locale strip, a mono-caps strip under the hero" — our banner is above the nav, not a strip under the hero, and it carries a real availability fact (not decoration). Fine. Gate 63: "decorative status dots" — none. Now, does the page need a dark-mode? No, it's a single drenched sheet. No toggle. Let me write it. One more: the pending tag is a span inside a flex li; `white-space: nowrap` so it doesn't break. At 375, contact rows fit. The `.links a` min-height 44 makes the label's hit area large; good. But the tag is outside the anchor, so the hit area doesn't include it. Fine. Hmm, the contact links are inert (data-pending). Clicking does nothing and screen readers still announce a link. Could add `aria-disabled="true"` and tabindex="-1"? The user wants display slots; a disabled link with `aria-disabled="true"` + no href would be honest. But `href="#"` + aria-disabled is contradictory. Better: use `Personal site` with a pending tag — not a link at all, just a display slot. The requirement says "hre f 写成 # 或留空" — they expect an anchor. Hmm, "可以用按钮、文字链或图标位，href 写成 # 或留空" — so an anchor with "#" is acceptable. Keep anchors with data-pending and prevent default. Add `aria-disabled="true"`? With aria-disabled on a link, AT says "dimmed"; the tag explains. It also signals a placeholder. But screen-reader users can still activate it. The JS prevents it. I'll skip aria-disabled (it would trigger 26b's "no aria-disabled anywhere" guard weirdly). Just href="#" + data-pending + JS preventDefault. Hmm, "fake send" gate 70 is about forms; no. Maybe the JS can scroll to the contact section for the hero Email? No, keep inert. Actually, a dead link jumping to top is worse than a no-op. JS prevents it. Good, small script: ```js document.querySelectorAll('a[data-pending]').forEach(a => a.addEventListener('click', (e) => { e.preventDefault(); })); ``` No success message. ✓. content.text:
# Hero review

You are reviewing the first screen of a page that is still being built. You did not build it and will not be told why anything is the way it is. Your inputs, and nothing else: the four `hero-*` screenshots, the stamp's first two lines, the Picks block's Material and Signature rows, and on a theme build the theme's picture. Batch your reads; stop reading by the tenth turn and write.

First line: `ship` or `fix`.

Then at most five findings, one line each, worst first. Ask:

- Does the headline say something only this product could say, in seven words or fewer?
- Is the content centred in the screen, or does it stop early over a band of nothing? Is the visual beside the text, a real picture (the user's, a photograph, the product built), and does it hold its half of the screen at 60% of its height or more? Where the shape puts no image in the fold (a Marquee, a Poster or a Banner hero), the type is the visual: does it fill the screen? At 1920 the container and the type hold their 1440 size by rule, so extra air there is not a finding.
- Does anything read as a template: a centred stack, a pill or a label above the headline, a gradient blob, an empty coloured box where a picture should be, a drawn illustration, a row of counting marks, two filled buttons side by side? A filled primary beside an outlined or text action that goes somewhere else is the control pair, and a sample of the product built in a slot is the product; neither is a finding. Grey bars or outline cards inside a slot are.
- Is the page's signature, its strongest real thing, on this screen? Delete the picture in your head: if the screen still says the same thing, the picture is too weak or too small.
- Does the type carry the theme at this size?
- With the theme's picture: is this first screen as finished as its first screen, in a composition of its own?

On a custom run (`theme: custom`) the composition is free: skip the centred, beside-the-text and 60% questions, and ask instead whether this screen is one you would expect a model to make for this prompt. If it is, say what gives it away.

On a redesign the page's content is fixed and what sits below the first screen is the old page, not yet rebuilt: neither is a finding. Never ask for copy, an action or a visual the page does not have; say in one line what the owner could supply.

What the theme file prescribes (its blooms, its control pair) or refuses is not a finding. Where the theme file and its picture disagree, the theme file wins over its picture. Do not fix anything.
======= FINISH
# Finish review

You are reviewing a built page against a fixed list. You did not build it and will not be told why anything is the way it is. Read the page, not the intent. Your inputs, and nothing else: the screenshots the render tier wrote (the folds at 1280 x 800, 1440 x 900 and 1920 x 1080, the full page at 1440 and at 375), the page's HTML or component source, the theme or idea line from the stamp, on a theme build the theme file and its picture, the hero review's findings with how each was settled, and `gates.md` § 4. Look at the screenshots first; open the HTML only to quote copy or to locate a finding; the linter has already read the CSS. A pinned pane shows once in a full-page shot: the column beside its later screens is the pin, not an empty half. Batch your reads; stop reading by the tenth turn and write.

First line: one of `recapture` (a screenshot is missing, blank or shows the wrong thing; list what to recapture and stop), `rebuild` (the first viewport fails the idea or the theme wholesale), `fix` (findings follow), `ship` (nothing owed).

Then the findings, ranked by cost to the page, at most eight, one line each: the gate or the plain defect, where it is, what you would do. Not findings: a direction you would not have chosen; what the theme file prescribes or refuses (its blooms, a glow on a theme with none); an element the hero review settled, unless you name a new reason. The theme's picture is the bar for finish and never a model: is this page as finished as that one, in a composition of its own?

Scroll the 1440 full page one screen at a time before ranking: a screen with nothing big enough to be its reason (a head and a line adrift, a narrow column beside an empty half, a section head under 40px, an empty coloured box or a drawn illustration where a photograph or the product should be, a row of counting marks) outranks every detail finding (`layout.md` § 8). Then the copy: name any head that would pass unchanged on a competitor's page (`craft.md` § 6).

Then one answer to the question no gate can: does the stamp's idea or theme describe the page in front of you? Name the largest gap, or say there is none.

On a custom run (`theme: custom`) the page owes no shape, composition or hero layout: it was designed from nothing, so judge it as a design, never against `layout.md`. Before the idea line, write two lines of your own from the screenshots: what the page is about, and the one thing a visitor would remember. Then three findings when they fail. **Seen before:** the page, or a section, reads as a template, a catalog theme or a familiar site; name which and where. **Clean:** something is on the page without a job (a device repeated, a decoration, a box around nothing), or a screen has nothing worth looking at. **Carried:** the idea lives in the hero and stops there.

On a redesign you also get the `before` screenshots, and the content is fixed: never ask for copy, an action or a visual the old page did not have. Add one answer: what did the old page do better? Name anything a visitor could do, read or find before that is harder now; if nothing, say so. On a polish you get only the full pages at 1440, before and after: the layout was kept on purpose, so ask one thing, whether anything still reads as machine-made, in at most five findings.

On an app screen (the stamp says `shape: app screen`) there is no hero, fold or section rhythm to judge, and the gates `flow.md` § App screens skips are not findings. Read the full screens at 1440 and 375 and ask what someone fluent in the category would: is the hierarchy clear, is the density even, does every control and table work on a phone, are the states there.

Close with one line naming what must not be diluted while fixing. Where the theme file and its picture disagree, the theme file wins over its picture. Do not fix anything.

3:Twenty-one named landing-page shapes. Each is a complete fingerprint (heading placement, body composition, divider language, button voice, image treatment, reveal pattern) bundled under one name. **This is a vocabulary, not a menu.** Design the page the prompt asks for, then name the shape you designed so Rotation and gate 32 have something to read; reaching in here first and building whatever comes back is how twenty-one shapes collapse into the same three. When nothing here fits what you designed, say so, describe the shape as a fingerprint (§ The fingerprint, below), and give it a short name for the stamp and the log (*a season page*).
4-
5-## The 21 macrostructures, index
6-
7-**Read only the one file** for the shape you landed on, from `references/macrostructures/`. Do not load the whole catalogue. Slugs are stable; Rotation reads the shape from the stamp and the log. Nav and footer are part of the shape, settled with the hero. Each shape file names the `layout.md` compositions it is built from; the code is yours.
8-
9-- **01 · Bento Grid.** Modular blocks of varying sizes laid out as an irregular grid. Each block is a feature, a figure, an image or a quote the user supplied. Rhythm comes from size variation, not card uniformity. [`macrostructures/01-bento-grid.md`](macrostructures/01-bento-grid.md)
10-- **02 · Long Document.** Reads like a memo, a letter or a journal entry. No marketing structure. Continuous prose with inline section heads. The page is literature about the product. [`macrostructures/02-long-document.md`](macrostructures/02-long-document.md)
11-- **03 · Marquee Hero.** The hero is the page above the fold. A single statement or visual fills the viewport. Below the fold the page becomes something else (a list, a grid, prose). [`macrostructures/03-marquee-hero.md`](macrostructures/03-marquee-hero.md)
12-- **04 · Stat-Led.** The hero is a figure the user gave, with the line that says what it means. Everything that follows supports or qualifies it. [`macrostructures/04-stat-led.md`](macrostructures/04-stat-led.md)
13-- **05 · Workbench.** Real product captures are the primary content. The page is a guided tour of the app in use, with short captions in place of marketing copy. [`macrostructures/05-workbench.md`](macrostructures/05-workbench.md)
14-- **06 · Conversational FAQ.** Bold questions, prompt answers. The page reads like an honest interview with the product. Each pair may be a disclosure. [`macrostructures/06-conversational-faq.md`](macrostructures/06-conversational-faq.md)
15-- **07 · Manifesto.** Polemical large type. The page tells the reader what to believe before it tells them what to buy. [`macrostructures/07-manifesto.md`](macrostructures/07-manifesto.md)
16-- **08 · Photographic.** A single huge image dominates each fold. Text is small annotation, not headline. The design says look before it says read. [`macrostructures/08-photographic.md`](macrostructures/08-photographic.md)
17-- **09 · Quote-Led.** The hero is a quote the user supplied, with its attribution. The headline is someone else's voice. [`macrostructures/09-quote-led.md`](macrostructures/09-quote-led.md)
18-- **10 · Specimen.** Large serif display, asymmetric spans, hairline rules, a typographic CTA, generous whitespace. Only for prompts about type, publishing or writing (a foundry, a journal, a press); the editorial genre alone does not qualify. [`macrostructures/10-specimen.md`](macrostructures/10-specimen.md)

82:## The fingerprint: six axes
83-
84-**1. Heading placement.** Left-margin (marginalia beside the body; a label beside a heading is an eyebrow, gate 54) · Hanging (the heading floats above in air) · Centred display · Bottom-aligned (the heading anchors the base, content above) · Overlapping (over a photo or colour block) · Sticky or pinned · Numbered by structure (a real `<ol>` with `counter()`, or one numeral at graphic scale) · Inline with the body (no break, the heading emerges from the prose). Any placement is fair; what reads as a mistake is a narrow auto-centred head over full-width left-flush content.
85-
86-**2. Body composition.** Single column · Two-column asymmetric (wide body, narrow margin for captions) · Multi-column justified with hyphenation · Marginalia (sidenotes in the outer margin) · Three equal columns (reference density) · Full-bleed with margin reset (65ch body, pull quotes and images bleed) · Asymmetric spans (2-1-3 ratios on a grid).
87-
88-**3. Divider language.** Hairline rule (0.5 to 1px, inset or full-bleed) · Ornament (a fleuron, a dot, a mark) · Negative space (the gap is the divider) · Bleed-colour block (a paper change is the edge) · Double rule. Pick one language for the page and vary its weight and placement by seam (9): the same rule at the same gap at every seam is the template.
89-
90-**4. Button voice.** Solid (one filled primary) · Outlined · Unstyled link (an underlined word) · Oversized solid · Typographic only (a word in a weight, no box) · Form as CTA (the action is fill-this-field).
91-
92-**5. Image treatment.** Full-bleed · Tightly cropped to the grid · Inline with the text · Margin-aligned · None.
93-
94-**6. Reveal pattern.** Fade-up stagger (once, orchestrated) · Horizontal sweep · Type-unmask (a clip-path opening over text) · Number-tick (counters, only on real figures) · Typewriter (a terminal only, the caret inside a typed command) · None.
95-
96-Fingerprint: one choice per axis, written `Hanging|Asymmetric spans|Hairline|Outlined|Margin-aligned|None`. Two rules: coherence (choices from the same world; a justified newspaper body wants a typographic CTA, not an oversized solid) and anti-repetition (no more than three of six axes shared with any of the last three logged entries; a None on Image or Reveal that the theme or the material forces is not a shared choice).

# Pi Agent Desktop **Your personal, minimalist Codex** — a native desktop client for the [Pi coding agent](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono), built with Electron for an experience that feels more native than the browser. [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Chasen-Liao/pi-agent-desktop?color=orange&logo=github)](https://github.com/Chasen-Liao/pi-agent-desktop/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Chasen-Liao/pi-agent-desktop?color=blue)](LICENSE) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Chasen-Liao/pi-agent-desktop?style=flat&logo=github&color=yellow)](https://github.com/Chasen-Liao/pi-agent-desktop/stargazers) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/Chasen-Liao/pi-agent-desktop/total?color=green)](https://github.com/Chasen-Liao/pi-agent-desktop/releases) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-blue)](https://github.com/Chasen-Liao/pi-agent-desktop/releases) [![Landing](https://img.shields.io/badge/Landing-GitHub%20Pages-111111?logo=githubpages)](https://chasen-liao.github.io/pi-agent-desktop/)
> **Upstream**: this project is derived from [pi-web](https://github.com/agegr/pi-web), with a focus on desktop experience polish and feature enhancements.

Sponsored partnership

Explore AICodeMirror and view its available models and services.

Learn more through my invitation link ↗

This link includes the author's invitation code. Service and promotion details are subject to the platform's pages.
## Table of Contents - [Features](#features) - [Download & Install](#download--install) - [Development](#development) - [Project Structure](#project-structure) - [Tech Stack](#tech-stack) - [Credits](#credits) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) ## Features ### 🖥️ Desktop Experience | Feature | Description | | --- | --- | | **Native desktop app** | Standalone Electron window with system tray and minimize-to-tray | | **Native workspace UI** | Apple-style layout, a liquid thinking orb, and a more compact message input | | **Auto-updates** | Checks and installs new versions from GitHub Releases | | **Shortcuts** | Ctrl+B toggles the left sidebar, Ctrl+Alt+B toggles the right panel | ### 💬 Sessions & Conversation | Feature | Description | | --- | --- | | **Session browser** | All Pi sessions grouped by working directory | | **Real-time conversation** | Stream responses live with the agent over SSE | | **Running message queue** | Enter to steer immediately, Alt+Enter to queue; drag or keyboard to reorder follow-ups | | **In-session branching** | Roll back to any node and continue from there, branches kept in the same file | | **Branch navigator** | Visually switch between branches within a session | | **Fork & clone sessions** | Branch from any node via API/UI, or clone to a plain directory or a Git worktree on a new branch | | **Session export** | Export a session to HTML or Markdown in one click | | **Model switching** | Switch models mid-conversation; picker loads providers dynamically registered by local Pi extensions | | **Usage & quotas** | Open the status-bar panel to inspect session tokens, cache usage, context capacity, and supported provider quotas with reset times |
